records.title: Transportation
records.description: Groups seven City aviation and transit performance charts covering flights, airport passengers and revenue, ABQ RIDE fixed-route ridership and productivity, and Sun Van ridership. Historical series shown through FY2018 or FY2020; the functioning reports do not establish current performance.
processing_notes: Discovered by deterministic crawl of https://www.cabq.gov/bikes/biking-in-abq.
Exact metadata and relevance remain pending source review.

2026-10-04 rendered live-application review: The functioning seven-report family supplies 95 labeled historical City transportation observations and measure definitions with material public value. Approve one grouped live directory with mandatory FY2018/FY2020 limitations; do not imply current monitoring or publish sparse members independently. Evidence: project-state/governance/interactive-app-resolution-2026-10-04/review-9.json

scope_assessment.geographic_institutional_scope: City Aviation and Transit Department measures of Albuquerque Sunport activity, airport revenue productivity, ABQ RIDE fixed-route use/productivity and local Sun Van ridership.
scope_assessment.specific_albuquerque_connection: Ninety-five annual observations concern Albuquerque airport/passenger revenue and City bus/paratransit services, with named City departments and measure contacts.
scope_assessment.abqinfo_public_information_value: Curated family exposes comparable historical demand/productivity series: fixed-route ridership peaks at 13,009,047 in FY2014 and ends at 7,670,422 in FY2020; per-hour measure ends at 19.3 and per-mile at 1.56 in FY2020; Sun Van ends at 197,256 in FY2020. This supports understanding long-run City service performance. Value resides in all seven charts together, not individual sparse reports or claims of current performance.
scope_assessment.general_context_exclusion_test: Direct measured performance of Albuquerque public transport infrastructure/services, not generic transportation context or incidental local statistics. A multi-measure time series has material public-information value beyond the index contacts and application shell.
scope_assessment.substantive_rationale: The functioning seven-report family supplies 95 labeled historical City transportation observations and measure definitions with material public value. Approve one grouped live directory with mandatory FY2018/FY2020 limitations; do not imply current monitoring or publish sparse members independently.

quality_assessment.document_function: Exact City ABQ View / ABQ Dashboard / Transportation directory, linking seven distinct anonymous-access IBM Cognos reports on newpublicreports.cabq.gov. Original directory URL preserved; resolved Cognos report IDs and paths recorded in render-22..28.json.
quality_assessment.substantive_content: Complete seven-chart family, 95 labeled annual values: annual commercial flights FY2006-2018 (13 values); aviation passengers FY2007-2020 (14); revenue per passenger boarding FY2007-2018 (12); fixed-route passenger boardings per hour, per mile, Sun Van ridership and fixed-route annual ridership FY2007-2020 (14 each). Report definitions identify revenue-hour/mile denominators, fixed-route versus paratransit trips and FY2010 revenue-hours methodology change. Charts are dense visual statistical records despite limited prose.

records.title: View a map of emergency routes and ineligible roadways.
records.description: Maps Albuquerque emergency routes, potentially eligible streets and City limits as a live geographic companion to the Neighborhood Traffic Management Program policy and eligibility process.
processing_notes: Discovered by deterministic crawl of https://www.cabq.gov/neighborhood-traffic-management-program.
Exact metadata and relevance remain pending source review.

2026-10-04 rendered live-application review: Approve NTMP Eligible Roadways as a live geographic component of the existing Neighborhood Traffic Management Program family. Real desktop rendering displays mapped emergency routes, potentially eligible City streets, current City limits and outside-City shading; zoom changes the mapped scale. The official current NTMP page links this exact app as its emergency/ineligible-roadways reference. It materially explains where traffic-calming policy applies and its emergency-access constraints beyond the textual overview. It is not an emergency navigation or guarantee-of-eligibility service: retain potentially eligible wording and program context, use one subordinate map link under the existing NTMP section, and avoid a separate redundant program entry. Evidence: project-state/governance/interactive-app-resolution-2026-10-04/review-5.json
